subject: model merging certification
statement: The paper proposes TwistedMerge, a conservative certification pipeline that separates fixed-chart averaging, synchronization-removable gauge inconsistency, certified central obstruction, and nonabelian holonomy for model merging.

subject: cycle residuals
statement: The paper reports that on natural checkpoint collections, cycle residuals do not predict merge degradation.

subject: descent theory
statement: The paper positions descent theory as a falsifiable certification and abstention framework for model merging.

subject: federated learning aggregation
statement: The paper proposes a lightweight and information-theoretically secure aggregation framework tailored for sign-based federated learning.

subject: secure aggregation
statement: The paper reports that combined techniques reduce online communication by up to 99.5% and latency by up to 85.7% compared to conventional approaches.

subject: dropout and adversary robustness
statement: The paper reports accuracy gains of up to 20.65% against dropouts and 10.74% against adversarial behaviors using MDS-code-based decoding.

subject: Deep Research reliability
statement: The paper investigates whether apparently credible but factually misleading knowledge can propagate through Deep Research workflows and be adopted as false conclusions.

subject: MisKnow-Agent framework
statement: The paper introduces MisKnow-Agent, generating 5,933 quality-controlled instances with controllable authority levels and styles for Deep Research tasks.

subject: Deep Research agents
statement: The paper shows that even limited exposure to misleading knowledge induces false-conclusion adoption in final reports of current Deep Research agents.

subject: gene expression prediction
statement: The paper introduces HierarchicalDAEW, a dual-graph architecture that combines domain-aware edge-weighted convolution with evidential uncertainty estimation.

subject: gene expression prediction
statement: The paper reports that HierarchicalDAEW achieves the strongest correlation with ground-truth expression across six human Visium sections.

subject: evidential uncertainty
statement: The paper shows that evidential uncertainty estimation produces far better calibrated confidence intervals than Monte Carlo dropout under identical conditions.

subject: anti-goal reasoning
statement: The paper extends Non-Axiomatic Logic with a corresponding definition of anti-goals to represent avoidance without treating it as pursuit of negated events.

subject: prevention operation
statement: The paper introduces a mental operation, prevent, to connect anti-goal reasoning with ordinary goal reasoning in cases of active prevention.

subject: radio map estimation
statement: The paper proposes RadioTrace, a novel radio map estimation framework that tightly integrates sparse measurements with a frozen pre-trained diffusion prior.

subject: transmitter location estimation
statement: The paper incorporates transmitter location estimation directly into the denoising loop, iteratively refining coordinates based on reconstruction quality.

subject: RadioTrace stability
statement: The paper provides a stochastic stability analysis showing that transmitter-coordinate refinement remains stable under perturbations from diffusion sampling.

subject: coding agent benchmark
statement: The paper introduces Tencent WorkBuddy Bench, a multi-domain evaluation suite for coding agents across Code, Web, Office, and Security domains.

subject: task construction
statement: The paper employs reverse-engineering from real commits and pull requests, rewriting tasks as colloquial requests to resist web-searchable contamination.

subject: coding agent evaluation
statement: The paper reports a cross-model leaderboard across several model families under uniform and reproducible protocol on two agent harnesses.

subject: diffusion model fine-tuning
statement: The paper proposes a source-prior-driven selective adaptation method that learns static masks to identify parameters suited for downstream adaptation.

subject: adaptation-retention trade-off
statement: The paper shows that the method achieves a better adaptation-retention trade-off than existing strong baselines.

subject: federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning
statement: The paper proposes TRISHUL, a spectral-control framework for robust federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning under non-IID client heterogeneity.

subject: federated PEFT aggregation
statement: The paper uses shared frozen multi-head low-rank bases to obtain algebraically exact aggregation of compact core updates across clients.

subject: federated PEFT performance
statement: The paper reports that TRISHUL improves convergence, stability, and final performance over federated LoRA baselines with greater gains under stronger heterogeneity.

subject: AI-assisted scholarship
statement: The paper proposes Traceable Scholarship as the minimum normative condition for valid AI-assisted humanistic research with clear sources and page numbers.

subject: page anchor methodology
statement: The paper introduces page anchors, dual page numbers, and citation-first generation as components of Traceable Scholarship infrastructure.

subject: AIH-Infra implementation
statement: The paper presents AIH-Infra as a three-layer reference implementation: Contexture, Open WebUI AIH-Infra, and AIH-Infra MCP Server.

subject: omni-modal distillation
statement: The paper proposes On-Policy Omni Distillation (OPOD), which routes each student response to the matching text, image, or audio teacher.

subject: omni-modal learning
statement: The paper reports OPOD achieves the best average score at every scale, reaching 70.8, 51.7, and 46.2 across twelve benchmarks at three sizes.

subject: modality balance
statement: The paper shows that on the 30B model, OPOD outperforms the base model on all twelve benchmarks and ranks first or second on eleven even when specialists are included.

subject: scientific interdisciplinarity
statement: The paper reports that after 2022, scientists increasingly published across more intellectually distant fields and entered new fields without prior background.

subject: AI-writing signal correlation
statement: The paper reports that authors with stronger AI-writing signals were already more interdisciplinary before 2022 adoption, and the gap widened further.

subject: research team division of labor
statement: The paper shows that contributors on papers after 2022 reported narrower role sets on average, with less role overlap and more fluid, distinct responsibilities.

subject: entity importance representation
statement: The paper introduces an interpretable dual-signal representation for entity importance: audience-evaluation dimension and structural-authority dimension.

subject: dimension association
statement: The paper reports a statistically significant but weak association between audience evaluation and structural authority (Spearman rho = 0.2275, p < 0.001).

subject: importance overlap
statement: The paper shows that overlap between dimensions is only 10% in the top 10 and 34% in the top 100, indicating non-redundant signals.

subject: source code summarization
statement: The paper proposes Transformer-Assisted LLM-Based Source Code Summarisation using task-specific Transformer summaries in prompt engineering.

subject: summarization quality
statement: The paper shows improvements of 7.8% in BLEU-4 and 5% in other metrics when combining Transformer-generated summaries with LLM-based generation.

subject: chemical reasoning hallucination
statement: The paper reports that across four reasoning model families and twelve chemistry tasks, hallucination is widespread and largely decoupled from answer correctness.

subject: chemical chain-of-thought
statement: The paper shows that chemical chain-of-thought functions as a hallucination-prone molecular scratchpad despite fabricated structural claims.

subject: SMILES perturbation
statement: The paper reports that perturbing SMILES sketches in Chem-R degrades generation, showing structural drafts are causally load-bearing despite inert verbal claims.

subject: edge intelligence framework
statement: The paper introduces Clustered Edge Intelligence, an intelligence-centric approach treating derived intelligence as independently manageable first-class entity.

subject: CEI architecture
statement: The paper presents a three-layer Clustered Edge Intelligence architecture for shareable, reusable intelligence across heterogeneous edge devices and applications.

subject: recommendation controllability
statement: The paper proposes the Controllable and Content-Based Recommendations framework, building recommendations from textual user profile representations.

subject: recommendation steering
statement: The paper shows that CCBR enables text-based and multimodal interventions, allowing users to steer the model towards preferred directions.

subject: recommendation performance
statement: The paper demonstrates competitive model performance with standard latent-representation models while providing controllable summaries via text.

subject: catheter-tissue interaction
statement: The paper formulates catheter-tissue interaction dynamics in the scalar tip-normal coordinate with configuration-invariant linear model.

subject: disturbance augmentation
statement: The paper shows that disturbance augmentation cuts free-space approach error by 90% in simulation of eight-link tendon-driven catheter.

subject: force-constrained control
statement: The paper reports that only the force-constrained predictive interaction-dynamics controller holds 0.47N contact force at identical tracking performance.
